pr.title: Follow a site's password rules with --rules
pr.head: b36192dc659212830797d9fbd1de7165beb9a41f

summary: multipass can generate a new password, either printed by multipass generate or stored straight into an entry by multipass add <name> --generate. Many sites limit what a password may hold: a length range, a required digit, only certain symbols. Writing those limits as separate options by hand is slow and easy to get wrong.

This pull request adds --rules, which takes a site's limits as one line in the language Apple defined for the passwordrules HTML attribute. Apple publishes such lines for many sites in its password-manager-resources repository, so a user can often copy one from there:
multipass generate --rules 'minlength: 8; maxlength: 16; required: lower; required: upper; required: digit; allowed: [-!#$]; max-consecutive: 2;'

The change has two parts. A new parser, src/generate_rules.rs, reads the line into sets of characters and limits. generator::Options then turns those into the recipe the generator in crypto::generate already draws from. The generator itself does not change. It still draws whole passwords uniformly and draws again when one breaks a rule, and it still reports a strength that counts exactly the passwords that follow the rules.

This is the top layer of a stack: generation itself (#23), then made-up syllables (#24), then this. The owner has decided to keep --rules, and the plan beneath this layer is now at status: ready with every open question answered.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Rule. One name: value statement, such as required: digit. Statements are separated by ;.
  • Class. A named set of characters (upper, lower, digit, special, ascii-printable), or a custom set in brackets such as [-!#$].
  • Requirement. One required rule. The password must hold at least one character from the classes it names.
  • Cell. A group of allowed characters that meet exactly the same requirements. The generator needs cells that never share a character.
  • Acceptance. The share of uniformly drawn strings that follow every rule. The generator refuses a recipe whose acceptance is below one in a million.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
The first Projector review, of cd0d510, found that a max-consecutive value of 2^63 + 129 or more made the generator loop forever, and suggested clearer README wording for required. eacd02d was the same commit rebased onto the moved base.

At 1c1a6cc, one commit drops a run limit the password cannot reach, with a regression test, and one rewords the README. The finding is resolved as fixed, and that head was signed off clean.

Since then, 5094bd9 and afc6b8d have rebased the layer onto moved bases. The layer's code is unchanged, and the README table keeps the --rules row beside the base's new --words default. The base now also clamps the run limit in crypto::generate::run_limit, from #23. afc6b8d was signed off clean.

e29c1cc added a plan line about dropping the layer and was signed off clean. aeae154 rebases onto a base that records the owner's decision to keep --rules. The rebase drops that commit and both "awaits the owner" sentences, and leaves the code unchanged. It is signed off clean.

b36192d rebases onto a base that brings in main's installer, release, and website work. It also trims the comment above the filter to the reason it still has, which takes the last suggestion. CI's test job passes, and the head is signed off clean with no suggestion left.

groups.title: Reading the rules
groups.kicker: A strict parser for Apple's password rules language
intro: generate_rules::parse turns the rules text into a Rules value: one character set per required rule, the set of every character the password may hold, and the length and run limits. It follows Apple's reference parser, PasswordRulesParser.js, in how it combines rules. The allowed characters are the union of every required and allowed class, or every printable character when no class is named. The largest minlength wins, and the smallest maxlength and max-consecutive.

Where Apple's parser skips input it cannot read and carries on, this one stops with an error that names the problem, because a silently dropped character would change what the password may hold. It also refuses unicode (multipass draws only ASCII) and the newer max-repeating and max-sequential rules, whose meaning the plan could not confirm. The rules are public text, so the parser may branch on every byte. The constant-time rule in the repository's guidelines covers only src/crypto and src/age.rs.

checks.text: The class definitions match Apple's parser, which the reviewer read: special is all 32 ASCII punctuation characters plus the space, and class names ignore case while rule names do not.

files.note: New. Splits the text at each ; outside brackets, then reads each rule's name and value. The tests at the bottom cover the plan's example, two of Apple's examples, repeated rules, custom classes, and one refusal for each kind of bad input.

checks.text: A custom class ends at the first ] followed by the end of the text, a space, a comma, or a semicolon. So ]] at the end of a class is a literal ], and a - is allowed only as the first character.
integer accepts any value that fits in a usize. Apple's parser ignores values above 2^53. rules_recipe drops a max-consecutive of at least the length, so a huge value never reaches the draw.

The reviewer ran a release build on 12 malformed or unsatisfiable rule strings, such as an unclosed bracket, an unknown rule, [a-z], and required: []. Each one exited at once with an error that names the problem.

groups.title: Turning rules into a recipe
groups.kicker: Cells, length, and run limit for the existing generator
intro: Options::rules_recipe builds the Chars recipe the generator draws from. It refuses --no-uppercase, --no-lowercase, --no-digits, --no-symbols and --symbols next to --rules, because the rules already say which characters to use. --exclude and --no-lookalikes still remove characters. The length is --length, or 20, moved inside the rules' bounds and multipass's own 4 to 128. The space is never drawn, because a space at either end of a password is easy to lose when it is pasted.

Two required classes can share characters: in required: upper; required: [-A], the A meets both. The generator counts strength exactly only when its cells never share a character, so the recipe groups each allowed character by which requirements it meets. Here that gives one cell for A (meets both), one for the other capitals, one for -, and so on. The strength count grows with 2 to the number of requirements, so at most 8 required rules are accepted.

checks.text: The strength count stays exact when classes overlap. For required: upper; required: [-A]; maxlength: 4; allowed: lower, counting by inclusion and exclusion gives 1,050,815 passwords, or 20.003 bits, and the release build printed 20.0 bits.

Drawing stays unbiased: the generator still draws every character uniformly from the whole allowed set and redraws a whole password that breaks a rule. It never places required characters first and shuffles.

files.note: Adds the rules option, rules_recipe, and an excluded helper shared with the existing character-set path. The strength line says with rules when the recipe did not come from the set options.

checks.text: A limit of at least the length is dropped, since no run can be longer than the password. With the release build, max-consecutive: 18446744073709551615 and 9223372036854775936 each return a password in under 0.1 s, where the first head hung. drops_a_run_limit_the_password_cannot_reach fails if the filter is removed. The base's crypto::generate::run_limit now also clamps the limit inside the draw, covered by draws_with_any_run_limit, so the filter here decides the strength label rather than guarding against the hang, and its comment now gives only that reason.

The existing check that refuses a recipe with acceptance below one in a million also covers rules. For example, five single-character requirements in four characters are refused, which a test here pins.

With the release build and a temporary store under expect, add --generate with the plan's rules stored a 16-character password that met every rule. Unsatisfiable rules, --rules with --symbols, and --rules with --words each exited 1 before asking for the passphrase.

groups.title: The command line
groups.kicker: The --rules flag and its help text
intro: main.rs reads --rules <rules> into Options like the other options that take a value, and adds it to the help text. The recipe is built while the arguments are parsed, so bad rules fail before multipass asks for the passphrase.

files.note: Declares the module, parses the flag, and adds a test that a rules line arrives as one argument and that bad rules fail parsing.

groups.title: Documentation
groups.kicker: The README section and the plan's account of the parser
intro: The README gains a table row and a section on --rules. The plan's § 2.3 records the decisions made while reading Apple's parser: what is refused instead of skipped, how repeated rules combine, how overlapping classes are counted, and how the length is chosen.

checks.text: The sentence now matches generate_rules::parse, which builds one set per required rule from the union of its classes: required: lower, upper is met by either case, and two separate rules need one of each.

files.note: § 2.3 now gives the space's place in special and ascii-printable, and lists how the parser follows Apple's and where it is stricter. The owner's decision to keep --rules lives in the base, so this layer no longer says the option awaits the owner.
